observations: Bruijns et al. Nature Neuroscience 2026 model learning with a dynamic infinite hidden semi-Markov model in which states have non-geometric duration distributions, can recur, and can slowly change; the study fits >100 mice and explicitly separates abrupt state changes from slower within-state adaptation.

Koppen et al. Nature Neuroscience 2026 show that cerebellar Purkinje-cell circuits learn prior probability distributions over temporal intervals and use those statistics in predictive behavior under uncertainty; this supports adaptive temporal priors as a neural computation, but not this worker's specific duration-controller algorithm.

Godin & Thivierge PLOS Computational Biology 2026 still expose S1 Code as Code.zip for SPLiT; public article transport continues to expose the supporting-code link but did not yield file-level source contents in this invocation.

bounded_audit.status: identity_anchored_duration_submodule_completed; semantic_anchor_strength_sets_safe-use boundary; label-permutation symmetry numerically verified; non_reproduction

design.scope: Event-level duration-learning submodule downstream of an assumed event segmentation, not a full SPLiT or HSMM reproduction.
design.duration_model: Cause-specific Poisson duration experts initialized at means 22 and 7 events/steps, with a shared state-agnostic base used for low-confidence shrinkage.
design.identity_anchor: Independent prediction/emission prototype z with Gaussian cause means separated by delta and unit variance. Duration tables are updated only through soft semantic responsibilities derived from this independent anchor; duration evidence is downweighted when semantic anchor strength/support is weak.
design.calibration: Adaptive duration learning rate and semantic-support timescale selected on disjoint calibration seeds; held-out evaluation used 48 new seeds, 1000 events/seed.
design.decision_probe: Dormant-memory admission proxy uses P(temporary-silence)>=0.9; report true admission on silence and false admission on persistent change. No synthetic MSE utility constants were imposed.

label_permutation_identifiability.principle: With equal cause priors and no independent cause-identity observation, swapping the two cause labels together with their duration distributions leaves the unlabeled duration likelihood invariant. Duration alone cannot identify which duration expert semantically means temporary silence versus persistent change.
label_permutation_identifiability.safe_guard_result: At delta=0 the identity-anchored learner assigned zero duration trust and exactly matched the duration-blind Brier score 0.25 on the abrupt-swap regime, while the fixed duration-semantic model was catastrophically anti-calibrated (mean Brier 0.95337 across 48 held-out seeds).

interpretation.positive: When an independent semantic prediction/emission anchor is informative, cause-specific duration priors can be updated online without committing to stale duration semantics. In the abrupt-swap probe, the adaptive learner recovered the reversed duration ordering in about 30 events at delta=1 and 17 events at delta=1.5, substantially reducing Brier error relative to both a fixed-duration model and a duration-blind model.
interpretation.negative_boundary: The benefit scales strongly with independent cause-identity information. With no semantic anchor, duration semantics are label-permutation unidentifiable and the safe behavior is to collapse duration trust to the shared/blind model. Even with delta=1, the adaptive learner remains far from the supervised oracle and sacrifices some matched-regime performance relative to a correctly specified fixed duration model. Duration adaptation does not solve emission/prototype identity drift by itself.
interpretation.memory_controller_implication: A dormant-memory controller should not treat duration statistics as a semantic cause label. Duration should act as a conditional prior only when an independent emission/prediction prototype anchors cause identity; otherwise shrink duration evidence toward a state-agnostic base. Tracker-specific utility calibration remains necessary.

limits: Synthetic bounded event-level causal control; not a reproduction of SPLiT, Bruijns et al., or Koppen et al.
Event boundaries are assumed known; full online segmentation remains unresolved.
Identity prototype separation delta is controlled and stationary in this audit; emission-prototype drift/crossing remains untested for the adaptive duration learner.
Cause-specific durations are Poisson in this probe rather than flexible non-geometric histograms or neural duration distributions.
Memory-admission metrics are posterior decision rates only; no new post-silence/post-switch tracker MSE was generated in this invocation.
SPLiT S1 Code file-level source remains unrecovered from public transport.
